storm_portland_corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY EXPLAINED — and the task's directional premise is half-wrong. The acquired odds do NOT show Seattle favored or the worse team priced as a coin flip: Portland is the HOME FAVORITE ~ -1.5 / -125 to -130 (Seattle +106; Portland ~56% implied; SI, sportsgambler). So the true divergence is model ~74-80% (Massey #12 vs SEA #15) vs market ~56% for Portland — the model is far more confident in the SAME side the market already favors. Injuries explain PART of the gap, not most of it: (a) Portland's season power rating is inflated by games that featured Sarah Ashlee Barker and Sania Feagin (both now season-ending ACLs) plus Karlie Samuelson (foot, OUT), with Oblak/Carleton/Puoch day-to-day — a genuine stale-HIGH input the injury-blind Massey/log5 cannot see, and it should pull the model DOWN toward the market. (b) But the dominant driver is structural: a 3-rung rating gap between two weak teams (POR 12-19, SEA 6-27) simply does not map to 74-80% in one high-variance WNBA game, and -125/-130 is normal moneyline compression. There is NO Seattle catalyst (no trade, no returning star; 10-game skid, 2-16 SU road, ~-11 road net, finishing a cross-country trip); situational edges (home, no travel, healthy/hot Carla Leite) favor Portland, and SI calls Portland UNDERVALUED ("should be favored by more"). HONEST VERDICT: the divergence is mostly MODEL OVERCONFIDENCE — log5/Massey over-mapping a small rating edge between two bad teams — PLUS a real but secondary stale-rating effect from Portland's injuries. It is not an unexplained market signal and not a hidden Seattle value; the correct read narrows Portland toward the market rather than backing Seattle. Caveat: the 56% and 74-80% figures are betting-preview snippets, not a clean odds feed or the model's own output — verify posted odds and the single-snippet day-to-day statuses against the official 5pm-prior WNBA report.
